mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past month compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months where FEDFUNDS declined by at least 0.1 percentage points from the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5.2% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes a recession and causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.2%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures indicates a broad-based weakening in aggregate demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where both HOUST and RSAFS decline from the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply shock regime (defined by a sharp decline in industrial production), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns due to reduced corporate profitability and increased uncertainty.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO falls below 105.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases the cost of capital and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate combined with declining real consumption expenditures indicates a weakening labor market and reduced consumer spending, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE rises and RSAFS falls from the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (defined by real consumption expenditures above 350,000 million dollars and housing starts above 2,000 thousand units), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns due to overvaluation and the anticipation of monetary policy tightening.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS > 350000 and HOUST > 2000.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index indicates strengthening supply conditions and economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months where INDPRO rises from the prior month.
